bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Segment concentration in Prefab / Buildings — The Prefab / Buildings segment contributed approximately 90.6% of revenue from operations in FY 2025-26, with EPS Beads at 9.4%, so group performance is largely a function of a single business vertical. Evidence read in the Corporate Overview section of the profile bundle, not in a risk section (no Risks & Concerns or Risk Management chapter reached any bundle of this annual report).
- Low sandwich panel capacity utilisation — Management itself flags panel utilisation of 44.1% in FY 26 as the clearest margin opportunity in the business, having restructured the leadership of that line; until utilisation rises the newly built panel capacity dilutes returns. Read in the Strategic Priorities spread carried by the strategy_outlook and capex_expansion bundles.
- Execution risk on a large simultaneous capacity build-out — Three plants were under construction at 31 March 2026 and the Company must take PEB capacity from about 147,122 MTPA to 220,000 MTPA and commission the Ghiloth panel line by around October 2026, all inside FY 27; the FY 27 revenue, margin and return targets depend on that timeline holding. Read in the Strategic Priorities and Capital Allocation spreads.
- Return ratios diluted by undeployed IPO capital — The Company itself notes FY 26 ROCE and ROE reflect fresh IPO equity not yet fully deployed into productive assets, with Rs 145 crore of the Rs 300 crore raised still undeployed at 31 March 2026 and held in a bank fixed deposit; improvement is conditional on Gujarat and Ghiloth reaching run-rate utilisation. Read in the Capital Allocation spread.
- Order-book dependence and lumpy project revenue — The Pre-Fab business runs on a pending order book (Rs 1,113 crore at 31 March 2026, calculated as ongoing contract value less work invoiced) rather than recurring sales, while the EPS Packaging business has no pre-specified orders at all and works on a roll-out plan basis as and when customers require, so visibility in that segment is limited. Read in the Chairman/MD message carried by the profile bundle.
- End-market concentration in policy-dependent capex cycles — Growth is targeted at renewable energy, data centres, semiconductors and electronics, EV and battery plants and cold chain, several of which depend on government PLI schemes and installation targets; the Company states it has no completed semiconductor projects to date and only a first data centre project executed, so that pipeline is unproven. Read in the Sector Deep-Dive spread.
- Workforce attrition and dependence on contract labour — Attrition of employees on rolls is disclosed as rising from 54.37% to 65.39% between FY 2025 and FY 2026, and the reported headcount of 3,515+ explicitly includes contract labour, permanent employees including labours and other staff. Read in the People KPIs table of the KPI scorecard.
- Governance and compliance exception - stock exchange penalty — The Corporate Governance Report affirms compliance with Regulations 17 to 27 and Regulation 46(2) clauses (b) to (i) and (t) read with Schedule V of the SEBI Listing Regulations 'except for the penalty imposed by the Stock Exchange, as detailed in the Annexure to this Corporate Governance Report'. The annexure detailing that penalty did not reach any bundle, so the nature and amount are not available here. Read in the governance_entities bundle.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: EPACK Prefab ended FY 2026 with four operational plants and three plants under construction. The operational base comprises Unit-1 (EPS Packaging) and Unit-2 (PEB plus discontinuous sandwich panels) at Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh; Unit-3 (PEB) at Ghiloth, Rajasthan; and Unit-4 (PEB plus a Continuous Sandwich Panel line) at Mambattu, Andhra Pradesh, where commercial production at the expanded facility commenced during FY 2026 funded from IPO proceeds. Under construction are a Ghiloth greenfield continuous sandwich panel line in Rajasthan and a new PEB facility at Vitthalapur, Gujarat, positioned for the Maharashtra and Gujarat corridor and on the DMIC and Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor, where one line is already operational. The Company ended FY 2026 at 133,922 MTPA of PEB structural steel fabrication capacity, added one line at Mambattu taking approximate capacity to 147,122 MTPA, and targets 220,000 MTPA by the end of FY 2027 driven by Gujarat Phase 1 and the Ghiloth greenfield. Sandwich panel capacity stood at 1.30 million sqm at FY 2026 against 0.51 million sqm a year earlier. The Ghiloth continuous PIR/PUR panel line is targeted for commissioning around October 2026 (described elsewhere in the report as commissioning Nov/Dec 2026 for the North India cold chain market), and management targets 70%+ panel utilisation at Mambattu by the end of FY 2027. Planned FY 2027 capex is approximately Rs 150 crore, funded entirely from internal accruals and remaining IPO proceeds with no incremental debt, against a stated expected payback of 18-24 months post commissioning. Of the Rs 300 crore IPO proceeds, Rs 155 crore had been deployed as at 31 March 2026 (inclusive of share issuance expenses), primarily towards approximately Rs 70 crore of term loan repayments and the expansion of Mambattu and Ghiloth, with Rs 145 crore remaining and held in a fixed deposit with a scheduled commercial bank. Three in-house design and detailing centres operate at Greater Noida, Hyderabad and Vishakhapatnam.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Renewable energy is India's fastest-growing construction demand: a 500 GW target by 2030 against roughly 220 GW installed today implies about 280 GW to be added in five years, and every gigawatt needs manufacturing infrastructure, warehousing and O&M facilities where prefab is described as the only viable method for remote, compressed-timeline construction
- India's data centre capacity is projected to more than double by 2027, with hyperscalers, co-location operators and domestic cloud providers building simultaneously; PIR/PUR panels specified for the thermal envelope reduce client HVAC load and operating cost
- The PLI scheme for semiconductors and electronics is catalysing greenfield fab investment, with cleanroom-compatible PEB shells and insulated envelopes as the entry point; no completed semiconductor projects to date, pipeline maturing into awarded projects in FY 27-28
- The new industrial capex cycle in EV manufacturing, battery facilities and power infrastructure, where a battery manufacturing plant and an EV two-wheeler manufacturing plant have already been completed as reference projects
- Grade-A warehousing in India is structurally undersupplied and PEB is the global standard for logistics construction; the Gujarat facility is positioned on the DMIC and Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor
- The government's PLI scheme for food processing is catalysing a multi-year cold chain build-out, addressed by the Ghiloth sandwich panel line for North India and Mambattu panel capacity for South India
- Sandwich panel utilisation of 44.1% in FY 26 is identified by management as the clearest margin opportunity in the business
- The pre-engineered steel buildings industry expanded at a CAGR of about 8.3% between fiscals 2019 and 2025, growing from Rs 130 billion in 2019 to Rs 210 billion in fiscal 2025
- FY 26 ROCE and ROE reflect fresh IPO equity not yet fully deployed into productive assets; management expects return ratios to improve as the Gujarat and Ghiloth facilities reach run-rate utilisation
- ICRA upgraded the long-term rating to [ICRA]A+ (Stable) from [ICRA]A (Stable) and the short-term rating to [ICRA]A1 from [ICRA]A2+, which management attributes to strong financial fundamentals and a stable outlook
- Management states there have been no deviations or variations in the utilisation of IPO proceeds compared with the objects stated in the Prospectus dated September 28, 2025
- Pre-Fab Business pending order book of Rs 1,113 crore as at 31 March 2026, against Rs 916 crore a year earlier and Rs 449 crore in fiscal 2024 - growth of 21.5% year on year
- Net order book of the Pre-Fab Business during the period was Rs 1,579 crore in fiscal 2026, Rs 1,209 crore in fiscal 2025 and Rs 704 crore in fiscal 2024
- Order book pending is calculated as the aggregate contract value of ongoing projects as of that date reduced by the value of work invoiced until such date
- In the EPS Packaging Business there are no pre-specified orders; the business works on a roll-out plan basis as and when required by customers
- Logistics and cold chain are described as sustained order book contributors, with Gujarat and Ghiloth directly positioned to serve them

risks.note: The Prefab / Buildings segment contributed approximately 90.6% of revenue from operations in FY 2025-26, with EPS Beads at 9.4%, so group performance is largely a function of a single business vertical. Evidence read in the Corporate Overview section of the profile bundle, not in a risk section (no Risks & Concerns or Risk Management chapter reached any bundle of this annual report).

Management itself flags panel utilisation of 44.1% in FY 26 as the clearest margin opportunity in the business, having restructured the leadership of that line; until utilisation rises the newly built panel capacity dilutes returns. Read in the Strategic Priorities spread carried by the strategy_outlook and capex_expansion bundles.

Three plants were under construction at 31 March 2026 and the Company must take PEB capacity from about 147,122 MTPA to 220,000 MTPA and commission the Ghiloth panel line by around October 2026, all inside FY 27; the FY 27 revenue, margin and return targets depend on that timeline holding. Read in the Strategic Priorities and Capital Allocation spreads.
risks.risk: Execution risk on a large simultaneous capacity build-out

risks.note: The Company itself notes FY 26 ROCE and ROE reflect fresh IPO equity not yet fully deployed into productive assets, with Rs 145 crore of the Rs 300 crore raised still undeployed at 31 March 2026 and held in a bank fixed deposit; improvement is conditional on Gujarat and Ghiloth reaching run-rate utilisation. Read in the Capital Allocation spread.
risks.risk: Return ratios diluted by undeployed IPO capital

risks.note: The Pre-Fab business runs on a pending order book (Rs 1,113 crore at 31 March 2026, calculated as ongoing contract value less work invoiced) rather than recurring sales, while the EPS Packaging business has no pre-specified orders at all and works on a roll-out plan basis as and when customers require, so visibility in that segment is limited. Read in the Chairman/MD message carried by the profile bundle.
risks.risk: Order-book dependence and lumpy project revenue

risks.note: Growth is targeted at renewable energy, data centres, semiconductors and electronics, EV and battery plants and cold chain, several of which depend on government PLI schemes and installation targets; the Company states it has no completed semiconductor projects to date and only a first data centre project executed, so that pipeline is unproven. Read in the Sector Deep-Dive spread.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: EPACK Prefab Technologies is a pan-India, end-to-end turnkey provider of pre-engineered steel buildings, prefabricated structures and insulated sandwich panels, listed on NSE and BSE on 1 October 2025.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Incorporated in 1999 and headquartered at Greater Noida, the Company designs, manufactures, installs and erects pre-engineered steel buildings (PEBs), prefabricated structures, light-gauge steel framing and insulated sandwich panels for industrial, commercial, institutional and infrastructure clients across India and overseas. It operates two business verticals: the Pre-Fab / Buildings business, delivered on a turnkey basis, and an EPS Packaging business making expanded polystyrene block-moulded and shape-moulded products for construction, packaging and consumer-goods industries. Manufacturing is supported by in-house design and detailing centres at Greater Noida, Hyderabad and Vishakhapatnam and a branch and marketing office network across North, South, East and West India.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Renewable energy is India's fastest-growing construction demand: a 500 GW target by 2030 against roughly 220 GW installed today implies about 280 GW to be added in five years, and every gigawatt needs manufacturing infrastructure, warehousing and O&M facilities where prefab is described as the only viable method for remote, compressed-timeline construction
- India's data centre capacity is projected to more than double by 2027, with hyperscalers, co-location operators and domestic cloud providers building simultaneously; PIR/PUR panels specified for the thermal envelope reduce client HVAC load and operating cost
- The PLI scheme for semiconductors and electronics is catalysing greenfield fab investment, with cleanroom-compatible PEB shells and insulated envelopes as the entry point; no completed semiconductor projects to date, pipeline maturing into awarded projects in FY 27-28
- The new industrial capex cycle in EV manufacturing, battery facilities and power infrastructure, where a battery manufacturing plant and an EV two-wheeler manufacturing plant have already been completed as reference projects
- Grade-A warehousing in India is structurally undersupplied and PEB is the global standard for logistics construction; the Gujarat facility is positioned on the DMIC and Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor
- The government's PLI scheme for food processing is catalysing a multi-year cold chain build-out, addressed by the Ghiloth sandwich panel line for North India and Mambattu panel capacity for South India
- Sandwich panel utilisation of 44.1% in FY 26 is identified by management as the clearest margin opportunity in the business
- The pre-engineered steel buildings industry expanded at a CAGR of about 8.3% between fiscals 2019 and 2025, growing from Rs 130 billion in 2019 to Rs 210 billion in fiscal 2025
- FY 26 ROCE and ROE reflect fresh IPO equity not yet fully deployed into productive assets; management expects return ratios to improve as the Gujarat and Ghiloth facilities reach run-rate utilisation
